author: DTrim99
body:
You're right — PE was missing the property-tax half of the 2022 Illinois rebate.

The Illinois Family Relief Plan gave two separate one-time rebates based on 2021 returns: an income-tax rebate ($50/filer + $100/dependent, AGI < $400k joint / $200k other) and a property-tax rebate equal to the 2021 property-tax credit, capped at $300, with a higher AGI limit ($500k joint / $250k other). PolicyEngine modeled the income-tax rebate (your $100) but not the property-tax rebate, so `srebate` came out $100 instead of $171.62.

The $71.62 showing up "twice" is expected — it's the nonrefundable 2021 property-tax credit on Schedule ICR (5% × $1,432), and the 2022 rebate is a separate payment set equal to that credit. So `srebate` should be $171.62, exactly as you said.

Fixes are up: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9420 adds the `il_property_tax_rebate` variable (= min($300, 2021 property-tax credit), gated on the $500k/$250k AGI limit), and PolicyEngine/policyengine-taxsim#1177 adds it to the `srebate` reporting. I'll ping you here when they merge so you can rerun.

(Side note: the issue title says 119K wages / 57K interest / 19K gssi / 3K proptax, but the scored input row is 38K wages / 28K pension / $1,432 proptax — the TA forms match the input, so just a mislabeled title, no problem for this analysis.)
